subject: Re: Pilot: swapping advanced dashboard seats for retention credits
messages:
From: Sally Nguyen <sally@dataleap.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot ask — can we trade dashboard seats for retention credits?

Hi Rafael,

Quick note after our product sync this morning — DataLeap is excited about Redwood's advanced dashboards, but the retention and tracing add-on pricing is adding up against our budget for Q1. We have predictable ingestion patterns but a large retention tail.

Would Redwood consider a swap: reduce the price (or grant seats) for Advanced Dashboards in exchange for a committed retention volume (e.g., 12 month retention credits)? Our procurement team prefers fewer line-items and a single committed unit to budget against.

High-level ask:
- Pilot: 3 advanced dashboard seats for 6 months in exchange for 80TB-month retention credits for 12 months (we can lock consumption forecasts).
- Short trial window first 30 days to validate dashboards for our observability team.

I attached a short usage snapshot so you can see our ingestion / retention shape. Can you route to pricing/legal and get back with a simple commercial path?

Thanks,
Sally
Sally Nguyen
Head of Observability, DataLeap
--
Attachment: DL-usage-snapshot.xlsx (xlsx)
From: rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sally Nguyen <sally@dataleap.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — can we trade dashboard seats for retention credits?

Hi Sally — thanks for the clear ask and the usage snapshot, that helps. Quick thoughts below and a pragmatic structure we can test in a pilot: 

Proposal (pilot):
- Redwood provides 3 Advanced Dashboard seats (feature-complete) for 60 days at no charge.
- In exchange DataLeap commits to a 12-month retention credit purchase of 80 TB-months, billed monthly or prepaid (your choice).
- Pricing: we'll credit the list price of 3 seats against the committed retention at an agreed conversion rate; if retention usage falls short we'll invoice the committed minimum.
- SLA & rollback: if dashboards don't meet the success criteria in 30 days, we revert to standard pricing and refund the seat credit pro-rata.

Action items for us to firm up:
1) Kimberly — can you confirm the conversion math (seat list price -> retention credit) and propose a conversion formula we can use in the SOW?
2) Marissa — any constraints on offering a 60 day seat trial with a 30-day success checkpoint from legal/commercial?
3) Sally — can procurement share target contract language or a PO cadence (monthly vs prepaid)?

I attached a short one-page commercial sketch (PDF) and will follow with a quick numbers email after Kimberly gives the conversion rate. I can also run a short dashboard demo for your observability team next week.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: proposal-dashboard-credit-trade.pdf (pdf)
From: rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: DL deal — need conversion, concession limits, and sign-off

Kimberly / Marissa,

Looping you in on DataLeap (DL-4921). They want to swap Advanced Dashboard seats for retention credits — pilot ask below. I sketched a conservative approach (60 day seat trial, 12 month retention commit).

Key negotiation levers we should evaluate:
- Conversion formula: how many TB-months = 1 dashboard seat-credit? I propose we start with a USD-equivalent conversion (seat list price / retention unit price) and add a 10% buffer.
- Concession cap: I can offer up to 25% of list price on seats in exchange for a firm retention commit without needing SDR. Anything beyond requires manager approval.
- Pilot SLA: 30 day success checkpoint where customer can walk away from seat discount if dashboards don't deliver value. Retention commit remains contractual (we can set a ramp).

Numbers request: Kim, can you run two scenarios by EOD — conservative (price parity + 10% buffer) and aggressive (price parity + 25% credit benefit) — include monthly billing vs prepaid economics. Marissa, highlight any legal contract language we should avoid (e.g., unconstrained usage floors).

Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Rafael
From: Sally Nguyen <sally@dataleap.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@dataleap.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — can we trade dashboard seats for retention credits?

Rafael — this sounds promising and reasonable. Procurement is fine with a committed retention purchase, they prefer prepaid but can do monthly invoicing with a PO cadence. Two asks before we sign:

1) Can Redwood include a clear rollback clause tied to the 30 day success checkpoint (we need language for our legal team).
2) Would Redwood consider an initial partial prepayment (50%) to reduce our internal approval friction?

If you can share the two conversion scenarios from Kimberly and the draft SOW clauses, we'll route to legal and procurement and aim to return a countersigned SOW within 10 business days. Can you also schedule the demo for next Tuesday at 10am PT?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Sally
Sally Nguyen
Head of Observability, DataLeap
